title: The Oldest Light
subtitle: The afterglow of the Big Bang

description:
Episode 22 of a daily journey through the universe. 📡
We find the oldest light in the universe: the cosmic microwave background, released 380,000 years after the Big Bang, discovered by accident in 1965, and part of the static on old TVs.

➡️ Tomorrow, Episode 23: Next stop, the Big Bang itself.
Start from Episode 1 "Leaving Earth" on the channel.
Follow so you don't miss a stop. A new episode every day.

segments.text: Episode twenty-two. Next stop... the oldest light in the universe.
Everywhere we look, space glows faintly with the oldest light in the universe. It's called the cosmic microwave background.
segments.headline: The oldest light

segments.text: This light was released about three hundred eighty thousand years after the Big Bang.
It was found by accident in nineteen sixty-five. Two scientists first blamed the strange hiss in their antenna on pigeons.
segments.headline: Blamed on pigeons

segments.text: Today it's incredibly cold, just under three degrees above absolute zero.
And a tiny part of the static on old TVs came from this ancient light.
segments.headline: In your old TV

segments.text: Tomorrow, we go back to the very beginning. Next stop: the Big Bang. Follow, so you don't miss episode twenty-three.
